scenes.anchor_text:
“Above silence, the illuminating storms—dying storms— illuminate the silence above.”
The above sample is noteworthy as it is a ketek, a complex form of holy Vorin poem. The ketek not only reads the same forward and backward  but is also divisible into five distinct smaller sections, each of which makes a complete thought.
scenes.scene_description: A visualization of the Ketek poem: dying storms illuminating silence above, implying a vast landscape under a celestial phenomenon.

scenes.anchor_text: The complete poem must form a sentence that is grammatically correct and  poignant in meaning. Because of the difficulty in constructing a ketek, the structure was once considered the highest and most impressive form of all Vorin poetry.

scenes.anchor_text: We leave it to His Majesty’s mind, on a strong day, to puzzle out the meaning of why the storms might be important, and what the poem may mean by indicating that there is silence both above and below said storms.
scenes.scene_description: A royal chamber bathed in soft light, overlooking a stormy landscape. A figure (His Majesty) contemplates the horizon, seemingly lost in thought about the meaning of the storms and silences.
